title: The Trading Day
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/0/body: **Day trading** means you **open and close every trade on the same day** and never hold a position overnight. Day traders usually work on the **5-minute to 1-hour** timeframes and take just a handful of trades a day.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/0/exampl: Usually 1 to a few a day
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/1/body: Since nothing stays open overnight, a day trader is safe from **swap** and **overnight gap and news risk**. In return, you have to be at the chart during **active market hours**, and your targets are smaller than a swing trader's, so **costs** and **noise** weigh more.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/2/statem: A day trader usually closes all positions before the end of the day.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/2/explan: That's the definition of day trading: start the day flat, end the day flat. That removes the risk of anything happening overnight.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/3/prompt: Which sentence correctly describes day trading?
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/3/option: In and out the same day, no overnight positions
Holding a position for weeks on the daily chart
Dozens of few-second trades on a tick chart
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/3/explan: Holding for weeks is swing trading, few-second trades are scalping, and holding for years is long-term investing.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/4/prompt: A day trade on the 15-minute chart. What's the risk-to-reward ratio?
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/4/explan: Risk: 1.0850 − 1.0835 = 15 pips. Reward: 1.0880 − 1.0850 = 30 pips. So it's 1:2. And whatever happens, the trade is closed by the end of the day.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/5/body: Day trading suits you if you can give **a few hours in a row** to an active session (like London or New York). If you only have free time in the evenings, **swing trading** on a higher timeframe usually fits your life better.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/6/prompt: Sara has an office job and only gets half an hour free at night. Which style is more realistic for her?
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/6/option: Swing trading with daily analysis and preset orders
Day trading the London–New York overlap
Scalping the 1-minute chart during work hours
Day trading with positions left open overnight
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/6/explan: Day trading and scalping need you there during active market hours. Swing trading works with half an hour of daily analysis and pending orders. And day trading with overnight positions isn't day trading at all.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/7/pairs/: Cost or credit for holding a position overnight
The active hours of a financial center
A price jump between the market's close and open
A trade still open after the day ends
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/8/senten: A day trader closes positions ___ the end of the day to avoid ___ and overnight gaps.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l1/steps/8/explan: Closing everything before the day ends means no swap fees and no surprise price jumps the next morning.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/0/body: A pro day trader has a **plan** before the first trade: the **economic calendar** (today's big news and when it lands), the **higher-timeframe trend** and **key levels** like yesterday's high and low. Without a plan, every price move looks like an opportunity.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/0/tip: Focus on 2 or 3 symbols. Following 20 means you don't really see any of them.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/1/body: Write your scenarios in advance: “**If** price closes above yesterday's high, **then** I look to buy the pullback. **If** it closes below yesterday's low, I look to sell.” That way, during the session you just **execute** instead of deciding on emotion.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/2/prompt: Put your pre-market analysis in order, from big picture to detail.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/2/items/: Mark key levels on the 1-hour chart
Wait for a trigger on the 5-minute
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/2/explan: The big picture comes first: daily direction, then levels, then scenarios. The lower timeframe is only for timing your entry inside a scenario you've already written.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/3/prompt: NFP comes out today at 8:30 New York time. What does a prepared day trader do?
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/3/option: Knows it in advance and opens no new trades near the release
Only finds out about the news after price jumps
Jumps in with big size right before the news
Removes the stop losses so they don't get hit
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/3/explan: Big news like NFP widens the spread and makes price jump. Being prepared means knowing the release time in advance and managing your risk around it.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/4/statem: For most day traders, focusing on 2 to 3 symbols beats watching 20 at once.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/4/explan: With only a few symbols, you get to know each one's levels and behavior better and execute your setups more precisely.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/5/prompt: Today's plan: “If price closes above yesterday's high, look to buy.” Check the last candle.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/5/explan: The last candle closed above yesterday's high with a strong body. Your buy scenario is now active and continuation is more likely. The lower-risk entry is usually a pullback to that same level, with a stop loss below it.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/6/senten: Before the market opens, check the economic ___ and mark the ___ levels on your chart.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/6/explan: The economic calendar tells you when the market might go wild, and key levels tell you where to expect price to react.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/7/prompt: Which one is a proper “if–then” plan?
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/7/option: If price closes below yesterday's low, I look to sell the pullback
I have a feeling the market goes up today
Whenever I see a strong move, I jump in fast
If I take a loss, I'll win it back with bigger size
lessons/day-trading-u1-l2/steps/7/explan: A real plan has a specific condition on the chart (a close below yesterday's low) and a specific response. Feelings, excitement and chasing losses aren't a plan.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/title: Prior Day Levels and the Asian Range
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/0/body: The **previous day high (PDH)** and **previous day low (PDL)** are some of the most important day-trading levels. Lots of traders watch them, and stop losses often pile up just beyond them. There, price either **bounces** or **keeps going** after a break.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/1/body: The **Asian range** is the high and low of price during the Asian session (roughly midnight to 7 or 8 a.m. London time; definitions vary a little). When London opens, price often **breaks out** of this range, sometimes for real and sometimes as a **fakeout**.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/2/prompt: The candles on the left are yesterday's, and from the “Today” tag on they're today's. Mark the previous day high (PDH) with the line.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/2/explan: Yesterday's highest price was the wick tip at 1.0880, so that's the PDH. Today price has climbed to 1.0874 and hasn't reached the PDH yet. Many traders wait there for a reaction or a breakout.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/3/prompt: The Asian range high was 1.0860 and the low was 1.0842. How many pips tall is the range?
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/3/explan: 1.0860 − 1.0842 = 0.0018, which is 18 pips. Many traders use the range height to estimate a target or size their stop loss.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/4/prompt: Tap the candle that broke the Asian range with a close above it.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/4/explan: The 8th candle only poked above the Asian high with its wick and closed back inside the range. This candle is the first whose body closed above the range high, and the candles after it kept going.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/5/statem: The previous day's high and low only mattered yesterday and play no role today.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/5/explan: These levels are on lots of traders' charts, and orders and stop losses cluster around them. That's why price often reacts to them today too.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/6/prompt: Price broke above the Asian range high, but the last candle is a bearish engulfing that closed back below the level. What do you do?
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/6/explan: A breakout that snaps straight back into the range is probably a fakeout: buyers above the high are trapped, and sellers' stop losses have already been taken out. A move toward the bottom of the range is more likely, with a stop loss above the high of these two candles.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/7/prompt: Yesterday's high is 1.0880 and the Asian range high is 1.0865. At the London open, price closed strongly above the Asian high and you bought. Where's a sensible first target?
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/7/option: I'll hold until the end of the week
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/7/explan: The nearest key level above your entry is yesterday's high, where price may react. The Asian low is in the opposite direction, and holding until the end of the week doesn't fit day trading.
lessons/day-trading-u1-l3/steps/8/pairs/: The high and low of the Asian session
Breaking a level, then quickly snapping back
